text:
Priya: kicking off pharos-mini-v0 onboarding to embed-staging. ran the usual holdouts (wiki, faq_holdout, support_longtail). overall recall@1 is down vs opal-base; interestingly the largest degradation is on long/paraphrase queries (>=25 tokens). posting quick summary and notes.

Jon: can you paste the summary table + exact eval command so i can reproduce locally?

Priya: summary (holdout combined):
```
model,recall@1,recall@10,avg_precision,cluster_purity,median_cos
opal-base,0.845,0.968,0.62,0.41,0.58
pharos-mini-v0-fp16,0.798,0.957,0.58,0.37,0.54
pharos-mini-v0-int4,0.736,0.939,0.52,0.33,0.49
```

Felix: hm fp16 hit ~4.7% and int4 much worse. did you use the same whitening/normalization pipeline as opal? any different tokenization or truncation behavior for long inputs?

Priya: used global L2 + whitening trained on wiki_corpus (same pipeline as opal). tokenizer is "canopy-tokenizer" default; it preserves clause-level separators which increased token counts for long queries slightly. no truncation, we keep full sequence.

Nadia: long queries being longer shouldn't alone cause recall@1 drops that big unless geometry is sensitive. could be that pharos's encoder compresses long context differently (kv pooling or layer scaling). can we run recall stratified by token-length bins (0-8,9-24,25+) and by paraphrase difficulty?

Priya: done quick stratification: recall@1 by bin (opal vs pharos-fp16): 0-8: 0.86 vs 0.84, 9-24: 0.84 vs 0.80, 25+: 0.78 vs 0.68. so biggest gap on 25+.

Rosa: suggests two immediate experiments: (1) length-conditioned whitening (compute whitening factors per length bucket) and (2) asymmetric int4 quant (per-channel + scale-zero) to see if int4 hit recovers. also try increasing PQ centroids in ANN index for long vectors.

Felix: i can prototype length-conditioned whitening and a small probe where we append length-normalized scalar to embedding (concatenate sin/cos length features) to see if classifier boundary moves.

Jon: also would run nDCG@10 and do a 100-sample human pairwise check for semantic relevance; automated metrics can miss paraphrase shifts.

Priya: command for the run i used:
```
python tools/eval_embeddings.py \
  --model pharos-mini-v0 \
  --holdout holdouts/wiki_holdout.jsonl,holdouts/faq_holdout.jsonl,holdouts/support_longtail.jsonl \
  --metrics recall@1,recall@10,avg_precision,cluster_purity,median_cos \
  --normalize l2 --whiten precomputed/whiten_wiki.npy \
  --ann-config index=ivf-pq,centroids=4096,pq_m=16
```

Nadia: i'll own the human pairwise (100 random longtail failures) and the nDCG run. Rosa: can you run the int4 asymmetric experiment + PQ centroid tuning? Felix: run length-binned whitening + length-feature probe. Priya: please retokenize longtail samples with the canopy "compact" mode (which collapses clause punctuation) and rerun to check tokenization effect.

Actions / owners / ETA:
- Priya: retokenize longtail with canopy-compact + rerun fp16 holdouts (ETA 24h)
- Felix: compute length-conditioned whitening and run probe concat-length-feature ablation (ETA 48h)
- Rosa: int4 per-channel asymmetric quant + PQ centroid tuning (small sweep) (ETA 48h)
- Nadia: nDCG@10 + manual pairwise eval on 100 longtail failures (ETA 72h)

Priya: initial note: end-to-end latency for pharos-mini-v0 is ~12% lower and GPU memory 20% lower vs opal, so if quality can be recovered it's promising for a compact tier.

vectorbot: scheduled job pharos-mini-v0/holdouts -> /logs/1769015000-pharos-eval.csv (ETA ~3h).

Jon: thanks. let's sync after initial numbers. :spiral_calendar:
